title: Last Stone Weight
oneLinerQuestion: Simulate smashing the two heaviest stones together repeatedly until at most 1 stone remains.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Last Stone Weight problem simulates a game where we repeatedly smash together the two heaviest stones until at most one stone remains. Suppose the two heaviest stones have weights x and y with x <= y. If x === y, both stones are completely destroyed; if x !== y, the lighter stone is destroyed, and the heavier stone's weight is reduced to y - x. Sorting the array repeatedly after each smash takes O(N^2 log N) time. A Max-Heap (priority queue) provides an optimal structure: extracting the two maximum elements takes logarithmic O(log N) time, and inserting the residual stone weight back into the heap also takes O(log N) time. By maintaining the remaining stones in a Max-Heap, each smashing round reduces the total number of stones by at least one, ensuring the simulation terminates in at most N - 1 rounds.

- Step 1: Max-Heap Priority Queue Initialization — Initialize a Max-Heap data structure. In environments without native Max-Heap implementations (such as Python's standard `heapq` or standard JavaScript min-heaps), push all stone weights negated (`-weight`) or configure the priority comparator in descending order.

- Step 2: Linear Heap Population — Insert all stone weights from the input array `stones` into the Max-Heap. Using standard linear heap construction (`heapify`), this setup runs in O(N) time.

- Step 3: Smashing Loop Simulation — Execute a while loop as long as the heap contains two or more elements: `while (maxHeap.size() > 1)`.

- Step 4: Extract Top Two Heaviest Stones — Extract the two largest stone weights by popping from the root twice: `const first = maxHeap.dequeue()` (the heaviest, $y$) and `const second = maxHeap.dequeue()` (the second heaviest, $x$).

- Step 5: Collision Resolution & Residual Push — Compare the extracted weights: if `first !== second`, compute the remaining stone weight `diff = Math.abs(first - second)` and push `diff` back into the Max-Heap. If `first === second`, both stones are obliterated, so nothing is pushed back.

- Step 6: Loop Termination & Final Stone Evaluation — When the loop concludes, the heap contains either exactly one stone or zero stones (if the final pair smashed had identical weights).

- Step 7: Return Result — If the heap has one stone remaining (`maxHeap.size() === 1`), return its weight: `maxHeap.dequeue()`. Otherwise, return `0`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N log N) where N is the number of stones, since each round involves two deletions and at most one insertion into a heap of size at most N, with at most N - 1 total rounds. Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space to store all stone weights in the Max-Heap priority queue.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION lastStoneWeight(stones):
    maxHeap = MaxHeap(stones)
    WHILE SIZE(maxHeap) > 1 DO:
        first = POP(maxHeap)
        second = POP(maxHeap)
        IF first != second THEN PUSH(maxHeap, first - second)
    END WHILE
    RETURN SIZE(maxHeap) == 1 ? TOP(maxHeap) : 0
END FUNCTION
